passages.text: Every wise woman builds her house, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
passages.sermon: A wise woman builds her house.\r\nA foolish woman tears down her house with her own hands.
passages.original: חַכְמ֣וֹת נָ֭שִׁים בָּנְתָ֣ה בֵיתָ֑הּ וְ֝אִוֶּ֗לֶת בְּיָדֶ֥יהָ תֶהֶרְסֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: He who walks in uprightness fears the LORD, but the one who is devious in his ways despises Him.
passages.sermon:
A righteous person walks in uprightness.
This person fears the LORD.
A devious person chooses crooked ways.
This person despises the LORD.
passages.original: הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּ֭יָשְׁרוֹ יְרֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וּנְל֖וֹז דְּרָכָ֣יו בּוֹזֵֽהוּ׃

passages.text: The proud speech of a fool brings a rod to his back, but the lips of the wise protect them.
passages.sermon:
A fool speaks with pride.
His proud words bring punishment to himself.
Wise people speak carefully.
Their words protect them.
passages.original: בְּֽפִי־ אֱ֭וִיל חֹ֣טֶר גַּאֲוָ֑ה וְשִׂפְתֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים תִּשְׁמוּרֵֽם׃

passages.text: Where there are no oxen, the manger is empty, but an abundant harvest comes through the strength of the ox.
passages.sermon:
An ox is a strong animal.
An ox helps people work the land.
If there are no oxen, the manger is empty.
People do not have food when the manger is empty.
A strong ox brings an abundant harvest.
People gather much food because of the ox’s strength.
passages.original: בְּאֵ֣ין אֲ֭לָפִים אֵב֣וּס בָּ֑ר וְרָב־ תְּ֝בוּא֗וֹת בְּכֹ֣חַ שֽׁוֹר׃

passages.text: An honest witness does not deceive, but a dishonest witness pours forth lies.
passages.sermon:
An honest witness always tells the truth.
He does not deceive anyone.
A dishonest witness tells lies.
He speaks falsehoods openly.
passages.original: עֵ֣ד אֱ֭מוּנִים לֹ֣א יְכַזֵּ֑ב וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃

passages.text: A mocker seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge comes easily to the discerning.
passages.sermon: A mocker looks for wisdom.\r\nHe does not find wisdom.\r\nA discerning person gains knowledge easily.
passages.original: בִּקֶּשׁ־ לֵ֣ץ חָכְמָ֣ה וָאָ֑יִן וְדַ֖עַת לְנָב֣וֹן נָקָֽל׃

passages.text: Stay away from a foolish man; you will gain no knowledge from his speech.
passages.sermon: A foolish man does not speak with knowledge.\r\nYou will not learn wisdom from his words.\r\nStay away from a foolish man.
passages.original: לֵ֣ךְ מִ֭נֶּגֶד לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּסִ֑יל וּבַל־ יָ֝דַ֗עְתָּ שִׂפְתֵי־ דָֽעַת׃

passages.text: The wisdom of the prudent is to discern his way, but the folly of fools deceives them.
passages.sermon:
A prudent person has wisdom.
A prudent person understands his own path.
A fool acts with folly.
Foolishness deceives fools.
passages.original: חָכְמַ֣ת עָ֭רוּם הָבִ֣ין דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְאִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: Fools mock the making of amends, but goodwill is found among the upright.
passages.sermon:
Fools mock when people try to make amends.
Fools do not respect repentance or forgiveness.
Upright people show goodwill.
Upright people act with kindness and favor.
passages.original: אֱ֭וִלִים יָלִ֣יץ אָשָׁ֑ם וּבֵ֖ין יְשָׁרִ֣ים רָצֽוֹן׃

passages.text: The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares in its joy.
passages.sermon:
A person’s heart knows its own bitterness.
No one else can fully understand this pain.
A person’s heart also knows its own joy.
No stranger can share in this joy.
Each person experiences sorrow and happiness in a unique way.
Others cannot completely enter into these feelings.
passages.original: לֵ֗ב י֭וֹדֵעַ מָרַּ֣ת נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וּ֝בְשִׂמְחָת֗וֹ לֹא־ יִתְעָ֥רַב זָֽר׃

passages.text: The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
passages.sermon:
The wicked build a house.
God will destroy the house of the wicked.
The upright live in a tent.
God will make the tent of the upright flourish.
passages.original: בֵּ֣ית רְ֭שָׁעִים יִשָּׁמֵ֑ד וְאֹ֖הֶל יְשָׁרִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיחַ׃

passages.text: There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death.
passages.sermon: A man may see a path before him.\r\nThis path may look right to him.\r\nBut the end of this path is death.
passages.original: יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי־ אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי־ מָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow.
passages.sermon:
Laughter can happen.
A person may laugh.
But the heart can still ache.
Joy can come.
But joy can end in sorrow.
passages.original: גַּם־ בִּשְׂח֥וֹק יִכְאַב־ לֵ֑ב וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ שִׂמְחָ֣ה תוּגָֽה׃

passages.text: The backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways, but a good man is rewarded for his ways.
passages.sermon:
A backslider in heart turns away from God.
He follows his own ways.
He receives the results of his choices.
A good man does what is right.
God rewards the good man for his actions.
passages.original: מִדְּרָכָ֣יו יִ֭שְׂבַּע ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: The simple man believes every word, but the prudent man watches his steps.
passages.sermon:
A simple man believes every word.
He does not question what he hears.
A prudent man watches his steps.
He thinks carefully before he acts.
He does not trust everything he hears.
passages.original: פֶּ֭תִי יַאֲמִ֣ין לְכָל־ דָּבָ֑ר וְ֝עָר֗וּם יָבִ֥ין לַאֲשֻׁרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: A wise man fears and turns from evil, but a fool is careless and reckless.
passages.sermon:
A wise man fears God.
A wise man turns away from evil.
A fool acts with anger.
A fool trusts in himself.
A fool is careless.
A fool is reckless.
passages.original: חָכָ֣ם יָ֭רֵא וְסָ֣ר מֵרָ֑ע וּ֝כְסִ֗יל מִתְעַבֵּ֥ר וּבוֹטֵֽחַ׃

passages.text: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, and a devious man is hated.
passages.sermon: A quick-tempered man acts foolishly.\r\nA devious man is hated.
passages.original: קְֽצַר־ אַ֭פַּיִם יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה אִוֶּ֑לֶת וְאִ֥ישׁ מְ֝זִמּ֗וֹת יִשָּׂנֵֽא׃

passages.text: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
passages.sermon:
The simple person receives folly.
Folly means foolishness.
The prudent person gains knowledge.
The prudent person wears knowledge like a crown.
The simple person lacks wisdom.
The prudent person values wisdom.
Knowledge honors the prudent person.
passages.original: נָחֲל֣וּ פְתָאיִ֣ם אִוֶּ֑לֶת וַֽ֝עֲרוּמִ֗ים יַכְתִּ֥רוּ דָֽעַת׃

passages.text: The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
passages.sermon: Evil people bow before good people.\r\nWicked people bow at the gates of righteous people.
passages.original: שַׁח֣וּ רָ֭עִים לִפְנֵ֣י טוֹבִ֑ים וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים עַֽל־ שַׁעֲרֵ֥י צַדִּֽיק׃

passages.text: The poor man is hated even by his neighbor, but many are those who love the rich.
passages.sermon:
A poor man has a neighbor.
The neighbor hates the poor man.
Many people love a rich man.
The rich man has many who love him.
passages.original: גַּם־ לְ֭רֵעֵהוּ יִשָּׂ֣נֵא רָ֑שׁ וְאֹהֲבֵ֖י עָשִׁ֣יר רַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: He who despises his neighbor sins, but blessed is he who shows kindness to the poor.
passages.sermon: A person who despises his neighbor commits a sin.\r\nA person who shows kindness to the poor is blessed.
passages.original: בָּז־ לְרֵעֵ֥הוּ חוֹטֵ֑א וּמְחוֹנֵ֖ן עֲנָיִים אַשְׁרָֽיו׃

passages.text: Do not those who contrive evil go astray? But those who plan goodness find loving devotion and faithfulness.
passages.sermon:
People who plan evil go astray.
They lose their way.
People who plan good find loving devotion.
They also find faithfulness.
passages.original: הֲ‍ֽלוֹא־ יִ֭תְעוּ חֹ֣רְשֵׁי רָ֑ע וְחֶ֥סֶד וֶ֝אֱמֶ֗ת חֹ֣רְשֵׁי טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
passages.sermon:
Every kind of hard work brings profit.
Hard work means effort.
Profit means gain or benefit.
Talking without action brings only poverty.
Poverty means lack or need.
Mere words do not bring gain.
Only effort brings true benefit.
passages.original: בְּכָל־ עֶ֭צֶב יִהְיֶ֣ה מוֹתָ֑ר וּדְבַר־ שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם אַךְ־ לְמַחְסֽוֹר׃

passages.text: The crown of the wise is their wealth, but the effort of fools is folly.
passages.sermon:
Wise people have wealth.
Their wealth is like a crown.
Foolish people act with folly.
Their effort leads only to more foolishness.
passages.original: עֲטֶ֣רֶת חֲכָמִ֣ים עָשְׁרָ֑ם אִוֶּ֖לֶת כְּסִילִ֣ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃

passages.text: A truthful witness saves lives, but one who utters lies is deceitful.
passages.sermon:
A truthful witness saves lives.
A truthful witness speaks honestly.
A liar speaks falsehoods.
A liar deceives others.
passages.original: מַצִּ֣יל נְ֭פָשׁוֹת עֵ֣ד אֱמֶ֑ת וְיָפִ֖חַ כְּזָבִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה׃

passages.text: He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge.
passages.sermon:
A person who fears the LORD has strong confidence.
His children have a place of safety.
The LORD gives security to those who fear Him.
The children of such a person find refuge.
passages.original: בְּיִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מִבְטַח־ עֹ֑ז וּ֝לְבָנָ֗יו יִהְיֶ֥ה מַחְסֶֽה׃

passages.text: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man from the snares of death.
passages.sermon:
The fear of the LORD gives life.
The fear of the LORD is like a fountain.
This fountain brings life.
The fear of the LORD keeps a person safe.
It turns a person away from traps of death.
passages.original: יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה מְק֣וֹר חַיִּ֑ים לָ֝ס֗וּר מִמֹּ֥קְשֵׁי מָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: A large population is a king’s splendor, but a lack of subjects is a prince’s ruin.
passages.sermon:
A king receives honor from a large population.
A king’s splendor comes from many people.
A prince suffers ruin when he has no subjects.
A lack of people brings destruction to a prince.
passages.original: בְּרָב־ עָ֥ם הַדְרַת־ מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבְאֶ֥פֶס לְ֝אֹ֗ם מְחִתַּ֥ת רָזֽוֹן׃

passages.text: A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly.
passages.sermon: A patient man shows great understanding.\r\nA quick-tempered man causes foolishness.
passages.original: אֶ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם רַב־ תְּבוּנָ֑ה וּקְצַר־ ר֝֗וּחַ מֵרִ֥ים אִוֶּֽלֶת׃

passages.text: A tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones.
passages.sermon: A tranquil heart gives life to the body.\r\nEnvy destroys the bones.
passages.original: חַיֵּ֣י בְ֭שָׂרִים לֵ֣ב מַרְפֵּ֑א וּרְקַ֖ב עֲצָמ֣וֹת קִנְאָֽה׃

passages.text: Whoever oppresses the poor taunts their Maker, but whoever is kind to the needy honors Him.
passages.sermon:
God made every person.
\r\nGod cares for the poor.
\r\nIf a person oppresses the poor, that person insults God.
\r\nIf a person is kind to the needy, that person honors God.
passages.original: עֹ֣שֵֽׁק־ דָּ֭ל חֵרֵ֣ף עֹשֵׂ֑הוּ וּ֝מְכַבְּד֗וֹ חֹנֵ֥ן אֶבְיֽוֹן׃

passages.text: The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin, but the righteous man has a refuge even in death.
passages.sermon:
A wicked man falls because of his own sin.
Sin causes the wicked man to be thrown down.
A righteous man finds safety even when he dies.
Death does not take away the refuge of the righteous man.
passages.original: בְּֽ֭רָעָתוֹ יִדָּחֶ֣ה רָשָׁ֑ע וְחֹסֶ֖ה בְמוֹת֣וֹ צַדִּֽיק׃

passages.text: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning; even among fools she is known.
passages.sermon:
A discerning person has wisdom in their heart.
Wisdom stays with the discerning person.
Fools do not have wisdom in their hearts.
People still recognize wisdom among fools.
Wisdom becomes known even when fools are present.
passages.original: בְּלֵ֣ב נָ֭בוֹן תָּנ֣וּחַ חָכְמָ֑ה וּבְקֶ֥רֶב כְּ֝סִילִ֗ים תִּוָּדֵֽעַ׃

passages.text: Righteousness exalts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
passages.sermon: Righteousness lifts up a nation.\r\nSin brings shame to every people.
passages.original: צְדָקָ֥ה תְרֽוֹמֵֽם־ גּ֑וֹי וְחֶ֖סֶד לְאֻמִּ֣ים חַטָּֽאת׃

passages.text: A king delights in a wise servant, but his anger falls on the shameful.
passages.sermon:
A king finds joy in a wise servant.
A wise servant acts with understanding.
A king becomes angry at a shameful servant.
A shameful servant brings disgrace.
passages.original: רְֽצוֹן־ מֶ֭לֶךְ לְעֶ֣בֶד מַשְׂכִּ֑יל וְ֝עֶבְרָת֗וֹ תִּהְיֶ֥ה מֵבִֽישׁ׃
